scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Crane's Path: The Semah of the Alevi
This is Semah, Alevi-Bektaşi ritual. 10th century to present.
on_screen: Title card: Semah, Alevi-Bektaşi ritual · Turkey · 10th century to present

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Semah is rooted in the Alevi-Bektaşi belief system, which is based on admiration for Ali.
It is a living tradition transmitted orally through generations.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is one of the twelve services of the 'Cem' ritual.
It symbolizes the unity of man with God and nature.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers perform in circular patterns and rotate around their own axes.
Men and women dance together.
The right palm faces upward and the left palm faces downward.
Watch for Turnalar Semahı.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Circular paths and center-oriented movements
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is played on the 'saz' long-necked lute.
The rhythm is typically the 'aksak' meter.
Listen for the saz.
The pulse is Aksak.
The music is characterized by the melodic, resonant sound of the saz lute, following the irregular, syncopated 'aksak' rhythmic structure.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned

scenes.title: The people
narration: Hacı Bektaş Veli is a central figure in the tradition.
Forms include 'kirklar semahı' (sema of the forty) and 'turnalar semahı' (crane sema).
Part of the broader Sufi tradition of 'Sama' (listening/remembrance), but distinct in its Alevi-Bektaşi practice.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Semah, Alevi-Bektaşi ritual is related of Sufi whirling: Both are forms of Sama, but Semah is distinct in its Alevi-Bektaşi communal practice.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Semah is a religious service within the Alevi-Bektaşi tradition. Outsiders should observe with respect and follow local guidance regarding photography and participation in 'Cem' rituals.
